id: TAHI: New Zealand Festival of Solo Performance--Wellington NZ
name: TAHI: New Zealand Festival of Solo Performance
long_description:
Comedy, cabaret, poetry, family-friendly acts, and world premieres are all on the radar for this theatrical event. The annual TAHI NZ Festival of Solo Performance provides a stage for more than 25 actors, celebrating emerging artists to experienced professionals. Storylines vary from rugby to the manosphere to an improvised nature documentary. Laughing and crying are both considered acceptable responses.

Tahi in Te Reo Māori translates to ‘one’, but another translation for this word is ’unity’. Dr. Sally Richards, director of TAHI, chose the name because of this duality. Solo theatre requires both personal courage and creative collaboration. As Sally says, “I see the stage manager, broom in hand, sweep before and after a performance. It reminds me that the solo performer is a misnomer — that solo performance relies on successful collaboration with others.”

Discover the brilliance of solo theatre at TAHI this September.

id: Wellington Home & Garden Show-Hnry Stadium, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Wellington Home & Garden Show
long_description:
Spring into your house projects with fresh advice from the best in the business at the Wellington Home & Garden Show. Bring your ideas to Hnry Stadium and get inspired to put them into action. Wherever you are in your home improvement journey, there's something for you. Explore kitchens, energy-saving solutions, renovating, landscaping, homewares, and more. Artisan goods, and health and well-being products are also on show. Take your time browsing the stalls, then attend an informative ‘Ask an Expert’ session. Legendary Newstalk ZB resident builder Peter Wolflkamp will make an appearance as well.   

If you need a brain break, go paint a pot with the team at Resene, or grab a coffee and bite to eat. Bringing the kids? No worries. There are family-friendly activities provided in the Springfree Family Zone. The show will also feature exclusive specials and giveaways, and one major prize.

id: Set Fire to the Brass-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Set Fire to the Brass
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Expect familiar melodies, unexpected turns, and a celebration of jazz. For two nights only, Set Fire to the Brass brings a two-part show to The Opera House. First on stage, say ‘Hello’ to Kiwi vocalist Joanna Darling. She gives English singer-songwriter Adele’s songs a lush, jazz-infused edge. She’ll give full-hearted renditions of hits like Rolling in the Deep and Skyfall. Members of the Rodger Fox Big Band and local musicians lead the second half with improv solos and classic jazz standards. 

Joanna has performed in musicals, cabarets, and as a soloist on international cruise lines. She combines a powerful vocal belt with piano and guitar. The Rodger Fox Big Band has played at prestigious jazz festivals and won six Tui Awards for the best New Zealand jazz recording. Together, they deliver the emotional depth of Adele’s lyrics with the warmth of live jazz.

id: Ford National Hockey Championship 2026-National Hockey Stadium Wellington-Wellington NZ
name: Ford National Hockey Championship 2026
long_description: For seven days, men’s and women’s hockey teams from across Aotearoa head to Wellington for a major competition. The outdoor pitches of the National Hockey Stadium will welcome dozens of teams in the Ford National Hockey Championship 2026. They compete across three tiers in the hope of impressing selectors ahead of the Premier Hockey League. Current and former Black Sticks play alongside emerging talent. Expect mouthguards, shin guards, and heated rivalries. Competition gets fierce when regional bragging rights are on the line.

id: Great Sounds Great-Various venues, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Great Sounds Great
long_description:
One ticket gets you access to ten venues and 40 artists. Great Sounds Great is back and it’s out to celebrate the alternative music community with the biggest party in Pōneke. The music and art festival will please everyone, from novice gig-goers to devoted music lovers. National treasure Bic Runga leads the lineup, joined by crowd favourite Savage, heavy hitters Beastwars, electro-pop Silicon, and Māori bass artist Mokotron. Artists will play iconic Wellington venues including Meow Nui, San Fran and Valhalla. Between sets, catch local poets spinning yarns. 

Eyegum Music Collective are the crew behind the festival. Established in 2021, Great Sounds Great is their flagship event and has grown in popularity every year. Looking for a warm-up? Eyegum created a mini festival named The Night Before. On 4 September 12 artists take over Newtown music venues before the action moves to Great Sounds Great in the city the following night.

id: Kevin Bridges — Here If You Need Me-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Kevin Bridges — Here If You Need Me
venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Punchy delivery and sharp social commentary are on the cards when Kevin Bridges heads to Wellington. His stand-up show ‘Here If You Need Me’ will have the audience at the Michael Fowler Centre laughing heartily. Kevin’s observational comedy has drawn more than two million fans across the globe. He’s built this through multiple live tours, plus radio and television appearances.

Kevin started performing in Glasgow after leaving school at 17. He made his TV debut at 18 at the Edinburgh Fringe. Since then, his tours have earned him Ents24 Fastest Selling Ticket of the Year and Ticketmaster’s UK Ticket of the Year. If you are a follower of UK television comedy you might have seen Kevin on ‘Live at the Apollo’, ‘8 Out of 10 Cats’, or ‘Mock the Week’. The Scotsman is flying over, and this is one comedian you’ll want to move fast for.

id: Lee Harris: The Oneness Experience-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Lee Harris: The Oneness Experience
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Follow your curiosity about the spiritual realm with the help of intuitive teacher and musician Lee Harris. For The Oneness Experience Lee is joined on stage by multi-instrumentalist Davor Bozic. Together they create a show that is part concert, part guided meditation, part unscripted spiritual teaching. Leave feeling lighter, wiser, and with the tools to navigate a changing world. 

Lee has spent more than 20 years working with people around the globe with his monthly Energy Update videos on YouTube reach millions. His approach is warm, practical, and funny (in a way you might not expect from a spiritual event). Every show can take up to three hours and each is different. Lee reads the energy of the room and Davor responds musically, so no two nights follow the same path.
